title: As If and I Wish: Como Si and Ojalá

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the imperfect subjunctive for imagined situations (*si tuviera tiempo*, B1 Unit 4), and you know *ojalá* with the present subjunctive from B1 Unit 3 (*Ojalá encontremos una solución*). This lesson adds *como si* "as if", which is new, and *ojalá* with the imperfect subjunctive.

sections.title: Como si: an unreal comparison
sections.content: *Como si* introduces a comparison with something unreal: the speaker knows that it is not true. The verb that follows is in the imperfect subjunctive, whether the first verb is in the present or in the past: *Habla como si lo supiera todo* "He talks as if he knew everything" and *Hablaba como si lo supiera todo* "He was talking as if he knew everything". English does the same thing with a past form ("as if he knew", "as if he were"), so the idea is not strange: Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive where English uses the past.

sections.title: Como si + imperfect subjunctive
rows: Habla como si lo supiera todo.
He talks as if he knew everything.
Me mira como si no me conociera.
She looks at me as if she did not know me.
Actuaba como si fuera el jefe.
He acted as if he were the boss.
Se sentía como si estuviera de vacaciones.
She felt as if she were on holiday.

sections.title: Ojalá: a wish that is unlikely now
sections.content: *Ojalá* with the present subjunctive is a wish that can still come true: *Ojalá tenga tiempo mañana* "I hope I have time tomorrow". With the imperfect subjunctive it is a wish for something that is not true now, or that you think is unlikely: *Ojalá tuviera más tiempo* "I wish I had more time". The imperfect subjunctive again marks the distance from reality, as in the English "I wish I had".

sections.title: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive
rows: I wish I had more time.
Ojalá viviéramos más cerca del mar.
I wish we lived closer to the sea.
Ojalá no lloviera tanto en esta ciudad.
I wish it did not rain so much in this city.
I wish you could come with us.

items.spanish: Mi compañero habla como si fuera el jefe de la oficina.
items.english: My colleague talks as if he were the boss of the office.

items.spanish: Me trató como si fuéramos viejos amigos.
items.english: He treated me as if we were old friends.
I wish I knew the answer.

sections.content: After *como si* never use the indicative or the present subjunctive: *habla como si lo sabe* and *habla como si lo sepa* are mistakes. The imperfect subjunctive is also what follows *si* in *si tuviera tiempo*. The *-se* forms exist here too (*como si fuese*), but *-ra* is the usual one.
